pr_title: Add CopyToAsync optimized implementations for StreamPipeReader
pr_comments:
Note regarding the `new-api-needs-documentation` label:

This serves as a reminder for when your PR is modifying a ref *.cs file and adding/modifying public APIs, to please make sure the API implementation in the src *.cs file is documented with triple slash comments, so the PR reviewers can sign off that change.

Thanks for the contribution @manandre. I'd prefer it if we didn't expose any code with the base implementation and instead optimized for calling as little functions inside of the CopyToAsync implementations inside of the `StreamPipeReader` itself.  

I expected the calls to CopyToAsync to basically enumerate from readHead to readTail and copy that to the underlying destination (PipeWriter or Stream), and then in the Stream case, delegate completely to the Stream implementation. For the PipeWriter case, what you're doing is fine.
This change is looking great! We need to figure out the tests.
I'm very happy with this change @manandre!
Thanks @manandre ! I will be looking for more Pipelines work to give you 😉

issue_context.title: Implement optimized CopyToAsync for StreamPipeReader
issue_context.body: The [`StreamPipeReader`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/6cde32922e8329c75b2db3e028c7b80b11afd0a8/src/libraries/System.IO.Pipelines/src/System/IO/Pipelines/StreamPipeReader.cs) implementation can be optimized by immediately writing all of the buffered bytes to the reader then delegating to CopyToAsync on the underlying Stream implementation.

review_comments: I think we want to move this to the top of the method and use tokenSource .Token everywhere.
These tests need to run for both the base implementation and the derived implementation. You can leave these tests here and tests with different PipeReader implementations.
One alternative would be to use TheoryData to pass different PipeReader implementations. The Pipe.Reader and `StreamPipeReader`

I have reused all the tests via inheritance.
I have removed the CopyToAsyncPipeWriterResume which I added in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/51147#discussion_r612795026 and which is not testing the expected behavior (see open issue #51272)
